title: How to read RizzitGO QC photos before you ship
summary: A warehouse photo can answer a surprisingly precise question if you know which detail to look for. Start with the style you ordered, then use the pictures to decide whether to ship, ask for another view or contact the purchasing agent.

sections.heading: Start with the listing you actually ordered
paragraphs: A product page can contain several kinds of pictures. The large cover image introduces the listing. A style thumbnail identifies one choice within it. A public QC photo can show an example of an item that reached a warehouse. Only the photos attached to your own warehouse order show what the agent received for you. This distinction matters particularly for listings that combine dozens of colors behind one cover image. A black shoe in a public gallery tells you very little about the white pair in your basket.

Before ordering, keep a screenshot of the selected thumbnail with its option text, size and quantity visible. Save the original seller link too. Open that screenshot alongside your warehouse photos later. Seller pages can change their cover image or reorder the options. A saved selection gives you something specific to compare even if the page looks different when you return.

sections.heading: Check identity before looking for defects
paragraphs: Begin with the easiest question. Is this the right item? For shoes, compare the overall shape, panel arrangement, outsole pattern and label size. For a backpack, count the external pockets and check which side carries the zip opening. For a two-piece set, look for both pieces and compare their color and size labels separately. A photograph of neatly folded trousers may conceal an entirely different jacket underneath.

Work through one order line at a time. If you bought the same model in two sizes, use the warehouse order references to keep the two sets of photographs separate. An image that proves a size arrived somewhere in your order may still belong to the other pair. When the label is too small to read, zoom the original image first. If the characters dissolve into pixels, ask for a close view of the actual label.

If an item has removable parts, make a separate count. A bag can match the listing in every visible detail while its detachable shoulder strap is missing. Look through all available angles before asking where the part was packed.

sections.heading: Read color and condition in context
paragraphs: Warehouse lights, shadows and the screen in your hand can affect perceived color. Try comparing neighboring parts of the item within the same photograph. On a jacket, do the left and right sleeves look alike? Does a darker patch follow a fold? Look for the same area in a second view. A patch that moves with a shadow suggests a different question from a mark that stays in exactly the same position across several angles.

For condition, inspect the areas most exposed to damage in transit. Look at projecting corners on boxes, handles where they join a bag, and toe caps on shoes. A small crease in a cardboard box and a split in the shoe beneath it merit different decisions. If the packaging matters because the item is a gift, tell the agent exactly which part of the box you want to see before asking to remove it.

sections.heading: Ask for a photograph that settles one question
paragraphs: RizzitGO describes warehouse inspection and offers custom photography among its services. A useful request specifies the item, the view and the evidence you need. For example, ask for the backpack to lie flat with both shoulder straps visible from their top seams to their bottom attachments. If one strap looked shorter in a folded photograph, that single view gives you a way to distinguish an uneven adjustment from a different construction.

For measurements, name both endpoints and the unit. For a sweatshirt chest width, ask for the garment laid flat with the tape extending from one underarm seam to the other. Compare that width with a sweatshirt you already wear, measured the same way. A tape around the entire chest and a flat width are different measurements. Check the ordering interface for any charge before requesting extra views, and keep your question with the relevant order.

sections.heading: Know what the pictures leave open
paragraphs: A clear photograph can show a crooked pocket or a missing button. It cannot tell you how a lining feels against your skin, whether a battery holds its charge, or how a sole behaves on a wet pavement. If one of these questions determines whether the product is suitable, ask the agent what can be checked while the item is still at the warehouse. A photograph of an electronic device switched on only documents that moment.

A good-looking label also cannot establish a product’s origin or authenticity. Decide what evidence you would need for the particular purchase before relying on a seller description. For a bag advertised with a laptop compartment, a clear view of the compartment and its dimensions will often be more useful than a close-up of the logo. Bring the inspection back to the feature that made you choose that item.

sections.heading: Make the shipping decision while the order is accessible
paragraphs: Finish with a brief note against each warehouse item. Record what matched, which detail remains unclear, and the action you want. A note such as “navy canvas, correct pockets, need a clear photo of the left buckle” is enough to resume the conversation without repeating the entire inspection. If you have several warehouse items ready, check which lines you select when creating the parcel so that an unresolved item stays out of it.

RizzitGO’s order guide describes warehouse review before the international shipping step. Use that point to raise a mismatch through the relevant order enquiry and retain the reply. Once you decide to ship, keep your selection screenshot and warehouse photographs until you have opened the parcel. If you later discover a problem, those records help show whether the detail was visible on arrival at the warehouse or only after the parcel reached you.

title: How to budget a first RizzitGO order across two checkouts
summary: A spreadsheet price is the start of a budget. Build the rest from the actual seller options, the destination and the shipping quote, then convert the total into the currency you will pay.

sections.heading: Put the selected style on the first line
paragraphs: Start with one row for each actual selection. Record the seller link, the color or model, size, quantity and price shown when you choose those options. A listing can group a single accessory and a full set under the same title. A low figure on a product card may describe the accessory, while the option in your basket costs considerably more. Check the option before you compare the purchase with another seller.

Keep a separate column for the currency. A number copied without its unit can distort the rest of the budget, particularly if one tab shows dollars and another shows yuan. If you use the currency switcher while browsing, write down the currency you chose. When you open the purchasing platform, use the current amount beside the matching style and quantity to update your estimate. Keep the original figure only if you want to see what changed.

For multi-buy offers, check whether the quoted amount is per piece or for the whole bundle. Compare the extended line total in the basket with your own calculation before applying any coupon or adding domestic freight.

sections.heading: Separate the order checkout from the parcel checkout
paragraphs: RizzitGO’s buying guide describes the purchase of goods and the later submission of a warehouse parcel as separate steps. At the first checkout, record the item subtotal and any domestic delivery shown. Domestic delivery covers the seller-to-warehouse leg. If two items come from different sellers, read each checkout rather than assuming one domestic delivery amount covers them both. Conversely, avoid adding delivery a second time if your displayed checkout total already includes it.

At the second stage you choose which received items to send, where to send them and which available shipping service to use. The international shipping estimate belongs to that parcel. Put it on a parcel row, then associate the items you selected with that row. This simple arrangement prevents a common budgeting error when three items travel together: adding the entire international quote to each individual item and counting the same freight three times.

sections.heading: Use an exchange rate you can explain
paragraphs: Write down the conversion direction as words. If one dollar buys seven yuan, divide a yuan amount by seven to express it in dollars. If your provider instead quotes a dollar value for one yuan, multiply by that value. Try a small amount first. At the illustrative rate above, seventy yuan should become ten dollars. This quick check catches a reversed formula before it affects your full order.

A display currency makes prices easier to read. The amount ultimately charged can also depend on the checkout currency and the conversion offered by your payment provider. Compare the total visible on the final confirmation screen with your running estimate and keep a copy of that confirmation. If the confirmed total already includes a conversion charge, record the total once. Only enter a separate fee when the payment record actually identifies an additional amount.

sections.heading: Work through a two-item example
paragraphs: Suppose you select a bag for 120 yuan and a shirt for 80 yuan. Suppose the first checkout shows 12 yuan for domestic delivery across those purchases. Your goods and domestic delivery now total 212 yuan. Later you choose a warehouse service priced at 8 yuan and receive an international freight quote of 110 yuan. Your estimate for the selected parcel becomes 330 yuan. These numbers illustrate the calculation and do not quote current RizzitGO prices.

At an example rate of seven yuan per dollar, 330 yuan is about 47.14 dollars. Imagine the final international freight line then changes from 110 yuan to 103 yuan, with every other amount unchanged. The updated total is 323 yuan, approximately 46.14 dollars at the same example rate. Keep the deposit and final freight on the same row, with a separate field for the difference. That way your history preserves both figures without adding them together.

sections.heading: Compare route quotes with the same parcel
paragraphs: A useful comparison uses the same destination, package contents and packing assumptions for every quote. Removing a shoe box can change the dimensions, but comparing a boxed estimate on one route with an unboxed estimate on another mixes two decisions together. First compare the routes using the same package. Then check how a packing change affects the route you are considering. Keep packaging that matters to you in the calculation.

The platform describes its freight deposit as an estimate and the final charge as tied to the verified parcel measurements. Review the terms displayed for your chosen service. Check whether its quote covers the costs you care about at destination or leaves some outside the amount shown. When a cost is still unknown, leave it marked as unknown. Putting a zero in its place makes an incomplete estimate look more certain than it is.

sections.heading: Reconcile the budget after dispatch
paragraphs: Keep the order payments, warehouse services, parcel payment, any account credit and the amount on your payment statement. RizzitGO’s guide describes a difference being credited to the account when applicable after shipment. Record where you see that adjustment. A credit visible inside a shopping account and a payment returned to a bank card affect your available cash in different ways, even when they have the same face value.

If you split a purchase with someone else, agree how to divide shared freight. Equal shares are easy, while an allocation by measured weight may suit a parcel containing one heavy coat and one light accessory. The split is your accounting decision. It should add back to the actual parcel total. Retaining this small record gives you a realistic starting point for your next order with a similar destination, packing choice and mix of items.

title: RizzitGO returns and after-sales help from warehouse to delivery
summary: A return enquiry is easier to resolve when it identifies the exact order, the stage of delivery and the outcome you want. Build your request around what changed and the evidence available at that stage.

sections.heading: Locate the order before you describe the problem
paragraphs: Begin in your account with the specific purchase. Collect the order number, original listing link, selected style and size, order date and current status. If the issue concerns a delivered parcel, add the parcel reference and tracking number. A shopping order can contain similar items, and several orders may share a single outgoing parcel. Keeping both references helps support trace the item without guessing which seller or shipment you mean.

Next write one sentence that someone unfamiliar with the purchase could check. For example, “I selected the navy cardigan in size M, but the warehouse photo for this order shows a label marked XL.” That sentence tells the agent what you selected, what you received evidence of, and where the evidence came from. It is more useful than a general complaint about an incorrect order. Save a screenshot of each screen you rely on.

sections.heading: Act on warehouse discrepancies before parcel submission
paragraphs: When a warehouse picture first reveals a possible discrepancy, open the corresponding order enquiry. Explain whether you want a clearer photograph, a seller check, or a return or exchange request. If the item has yet to be packed, keep it out of your international parcel selection while the issue is being reviewed. This is particularly important if several other items are ready and you intend to ship them separately.

Distinguish uncertainty from a confirmed mismatch. A folded navy cardigan might look black under warehouse lighting. Seeing an XL size label beside an order for M gives the agent a different question to investigate. For the color issue, a close photograph beside the item’s attached option label might resolve the doubt. For the size issue, ask the agent to confirm that the label belongs to your item and whether the seller can supply the selected size.
If the problem affects only one piece of a set, ask whether the seller needs the entire set back. Confirm that point before removing tags, discarding packaging or separating the pieces.

sections.heading: Ask what a seller return would involve
paragraphs: RizzitGO’s agreement describes assistance with problematic goods and the original seller’s role. Treat the outcome as order-specific. Ask what the seller has agreed to accept, where the item currently sits, which charges apply, and what action you must confirm in your account. If you changed your mind about an otherwise correct item, say that plainly. A request prompted by preference and one prompted by a documented shipping error can lead to different replies.

Before authorizing a return shipment, ask for the quoted amount you would receive and a breakdown of any proposed deductions. Consider a low-priced accessory that costs little more than its return freight. A successful return may still recover very little. If the seller offers an exchange, ask how the replacement option will be identified and whether a fresh warehouse photograph will be available before international dispatch. Keep the written reply attached to the same enquiry.

sections.heading: Document a problem discovered on delivery
paragraphs: If the issue first appears when you receive the parcel, retain the outer packaging, its shipping label, any inner packaging and the affected item while support reviews the case. Photograph the parcel as it arrived where possible, then record the damaged area or missing component clearly. For a cracked storage case, take a view showing the entire case and a closer view showing where the crack begins. The wider view identifies the object; the close view shows the detail.

For a missing item, check the warehouse parcel contents against the individual shopping orders. One purchase might still be in storage or might have been sent under another parcel reference. Once you have checked, identify the exact line that is missing and list the contents you did receive. RizzitGO’s buying guide directs customers with post-delivery issues to the relevant parcel in the User Center for an after-sales application. Review the options displayed there for your shipment.

sections.heading: Describe the remedy and keep personal details private
paragraphs: State your preferred outcome in a single line. You may want the correct size, a replacement component or a refund review. If your preference depends on cost, say so. For example, ask the agent to confirm the total cost of obtaining a replacement zip pull before you decide whether to proceed. Give support the necessary order details through the official account channel. Avoid posting a shipping label with your full address or phone number on a public forum.

When several pictures support the same request, put them in a clear order. Start with the saved selection, continue with the warehouse image, and finish with the delivered item if available. Explain what each photo shows in a few words. A receipt can identify the order, but an unrelated list of purchases adds little to the investigation. Check each attachment before submitting, especially if your camera roll contains similar items from different parcels.

sections.heading: Follow the case through the actual resolution
paragraphs: Save the enquiry reference and record the next action named in the reply. A seller agreeing to review a request, accepting goods back, dispatching a replacement and issuing a refund are different events. If an exchange is offered, verify the replacement size and color against the original selection when it arrives. If a refund is offered, check the amount, currency and stated destination against the resolution you accepted.

Where the reply specifies a deadline or requests another image, act according to the instructions for your order. A timeframe seen in somebody else’s review may reflect a different seller or shipping service. If the case stalls, follow up in the existing enquiry with the date of the last response and the remaining question. Close your own record only when you can identify the final result, such as a replacement visible in storage or a credit actually posted to the stated account.
